subject: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novahealth.com>; laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com; marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-01T15:04:00Z
Subject: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners

Hi Elaine / NovaHealth team,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — appreciated the candid feedback. Per our call, I put together a short "scout" playbook and the proposed next-phase owners so we can get the bakeoff scheduled and scoped. Attached: bakeoff-playbook-v1.xlsx (test matrix + initial timelines).

High-level summary / asks for NovaHealth to confirm:
- Primary goal: 99th percentile generation latency < 200ms for short clinical prompts (<=512 tokens) while preserving response fidelity for our diagnostics intent set.
- Secondary goal: token cost per request reduction vs your current endpoint by >= 30% at target throughput.
- Data residency: US-only for trial data (will require private routing).

Proposed next steps (timeline in the attachment):
1) You confirm success criteria and provide 1 representative prompt set (we can take sample or use yours) — target by Wed 2026-11-03.
2) Redwood runs baseline against our hosted model variants and two hyperscaler APIs (cloud-edge partner + public API) — 1 week sprint (start 2026-11-08).
3) Engineering validation run (latency/throughput + KV cache behavior) with assigned owners below; we deliver a scorecard and cost comparison.

Owners (proposed):
- Test design & dataset ingestion: laura_bennett
- Runtime config & quantization variants: marissa_cole
- Metrics, 99th/avg, and cost analysis: rishi_malhotra
- Sales/coord + timelines: me (Aditya)

Questions for you:
- Can you waive any production-style throttles for test traffic (we only need controlled bursts)?
- Any sensitive prompt examples you absolutely cannot share? We can accept redacted versions.

Thanks — I’ll stand up the ticket in Jira and share the kickoff invite once you confirm the prompt set.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachment: bakeoff-playbook-v1.xlsx

From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novahealth.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: contracts@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-11-02T10:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners

Thanks Aditya — clear and helpful. A couple clarifications from our side after we reviewed the workbook:

1) Latency target: 99th < 200ms for short prompts is reasonable, but we should also evaluate 95th and p50 across burst windows (we see spikes during morning ingest).
2) Data residency: US-only is mandatory for the trial.
3) Prompt set: attaching a small redacted sample (novahealth-sample-prompts.txt). These are short clinical summarization prompts and a few QA-style prompts (<=256 tokens).

A few asks:
- Can Redwood include a test that simulates our 50 RPS burst (60s window)?
- We also need to see behavior when KV cache is cold vs warm (important for sequential patient sessions).

We are good to proceed with the proposed owners. Please include a quick note on what quantization variants you will test (FP16, int8/awq or similar) and any expected quality tradeoffs.

If you need a formal NDA addendum or data processing addendum, loop in contracts@novahealth.com.

Elaine Park
Head of Integrations, NovaHealth Inc.
elaine.park@novahealth.com
Attachment: novahealth-sample-prompts.txt

Date: 2026-11-04T09:30:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners

Folks — forwarding Elaine's notes and the sample prompts. Action items below; can each owner confirm ETA?

Forwarded message:
> From: Elaine Park <elaine.park@novahealth.com>
> Date: 2026-11-02T10:18:00Z
> Subject: Re: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners
> To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
> 
> (see attachment novahealth-sample-prompts.txt)

My proposed owners & asks (please reply inline with ETA):
- laura_bennett: Test dataset ingestion & canonicalization (target: 2026-11-06). Need confirmation that NovaHealth sample ingest pipeline can shuffle & preserve token boundaries; will create test dataset in S3. Attachment: test-vector-sample.json (schema).
- marissa_cole: Runtime variants + quantization matrix. Please enumerate the specific configurations (e.g., FP16 baseline, int8-awq, int4 if safe) and expected quality delta notes. Deliverable: brief doc + runbook by 2026-11-07.
- rishi_malhotra: Metrics dashboard and cost model. Need 99th/95th/p50 latency, token cost, and per-request cost projection for peak RPS. Target: initial dashboard by 2026-11-09.

Logistics:
- Tentative kick-off for the engineering sprint: 2026-11-08. We will run 48-hour baseline tests and a 24-hour extended run focusing on burst windows.
- We need a short cloud request (I will open SUP-327) for capacity to run concurrent variants.

Please flag any blockers. I will coordinate scheduling with NovaHealth contracts if they request a DPA.

Thanks,
Aditya

Attachment: bakeoff-playbook-v2.pdf; test-vector-sample.json

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>; laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com; marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-06T11:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners

Agree to the owner assignments — allocating infra and dashboards. Quick notes:
- I will provision the metrics pipeline and a Grafana dashboard that reports p50/95/99 latencies and token cost by model variant. ETA for initial dashboard: 2026-11-09 EOD.
- For the burst test, recommend synthetic driver that reproduces 50 RPS 60s window and a second suite with realistic inter-request spacing to exercise KV cache.
- On cost modeling: need an estimate of model sizes and expected token counts per prompt from NovaHealth sample. If their average prompt is ~120 tokens and response 80 tokens, the per-request token count assumptions will matter.

I will also include a quick section on how quantization may affect p99 tail (int8 can add variance on heavy-attention paths). Marissa, if you can list the exact variants today I’ll wire up the expected cost delta into the dashboard.

Rishi
Staff Engineer, Runtime

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>; marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com; rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-11-10T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Scout report: bakeoff playbook & next-phase owners

All good from my side — final plan below and I’m confirming the kickoff calendar invite for 2026-11-08 16:00 PT.

Final test plan summary (short):
- Ingestion: laura_bennett will produce canonical test S3 bucket with 3 sets: warm-cache, cold-cache, and burst-driver sequences. Deliverable: test-bucket location + schema by 2026-11-06 (done).
- Runtime variants: marissa will test FP16 baseline, int8-awq, and an int4-safe profile (if model supports). Expect qualitatively measurable delta notes; record BLEU/ROUGE-style measures where appropriate.
- Metrics & scoring: rishi will publish a scorecard with weighted metrics (p99 latency 40%, accuracy/QA fidelity 40%, cost 20%).
- Kickoff & run window: 2026-11-08 to 2026-11-12 (48-hour baseline starting first day, 24-hour burst test on day 2).

Deliverables after run: consolidated scorecard, side-by-side transcript samples for fidelity review, and a short exec-level one-pager for NovaHealth procurement. I will send the one-pager and the DocuSign trial statement (link) for signature after the baseline completes.

Thanks everyone — Marissa / Rishi, please confirm when your runbooks are uploaded to SUP-327. Aditya, I’ll copy NovaHealth after we have the first scorecard.

Laura Bennett
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
